definition: A read-only package holding an application’s files and settings, used as the starting point for containers.
watch_for: A tag such as :release can be moved to a different image; a digest always means the same content.

definition: A running (or stopped) copy of an image, with its own isolated view of files, network, and processes.
watch_for: Removing a container deletes any files it changed, unless they were stored in a volume or mount.

definition: The main process inside a container. Docker sends it the stop signal, and the container ends when it ends.
watch_for: If a startup script launches the real server in the background and exits, the container stops too.

definition: A saved set of file changes. An image is a stack of layers, one for each build step that changes files.
watch_for: Deleting a file in a later step hides it but leaves it inside the earlier layer.

definition: The folder whose files a Docker build is allowed to copy, named by the last argument of docker build.
watch_for: COPY cannot reach files outside it, and anything inside it, including secrets, can be copied unless excluded by .dockerignore.

definition: Docker’s store of earlier build results, reused when a step and its input files have not changed.
watch_for: A cached step was not re-run, so it will not pick up changes from outside the build, such as a newer package online.

definition: A Dockerfile with more than one FROM, so tools used for building can be left out of the final image.
watch_for: The final stage still needs everything the application needs to run; copy it in deliberately.

definition: A fingerprint calculated from an image’s content, written like sha256:3f1a..., that changes whenever the content changes.
watch_for: One name can cover images for several processor types, and each of those has its own digest too.

definition: A server that stores images so other computers can push and pull them, such as Docker Hub.
watch_for: A successful push does not mean another machine has the network access or password needed to pull it.

definition: A folder from your computer made visible at a path inside a container.
watch_for: The folder keeps your computer’s owners and permissions, and it hides whatever the image had at that path.

definition: Storage managed by Docker or Kubernetes that lives separately from any one container.
watch_for: Surviving a container replacement is not the same as having a tested backup.

definition: A private virtual network that Docker creates so containers on it can reach each other by name.
watch_for: Being able to reach an address does not mean a name resolves, or that the app is listening on that port.

definition: A port on your computer that Docker forwards to a port inside a container, set with -p.
watch_for: The two port numbers can differ, and binding to 127.0.0.1 keeps the port private to your computer.

definition: One named part of a Docker Compose project, such as api or db, with its container settings.
watch_for: Starting services in order does not mean each one is ready; use health checks and have apps retry.

definition: A command run regularly inside a container to report whether it can do its job.
watch_for: It only tests what its command tests; a check that the process is up says nothing about its database.

definition: The part of Kubernetes that stores the cluster’s state, runs the API, decides where Pods run, and keeps everything in line.
watch_for: Existing containers can keep running while it is down, but nothing new can be changed or repaired.

definition: A controller’s loop of comparing what you asked for with what exists, and acting to close the gap.
watch_for: Submitting a change starts this process; it does not mean the change has finished.

definition: Kubernetes’ smallest unit of work: one or more containers that run together and share a network address.
watch_for: A replacement Pod is a new Pod with a new name and address; Services and controllers hide that from users.

definition: A Kubernetes object that keeps a set number of identical Pods running and rolls out updates to them.
watch_for: Its own labels and the labels on the Pods it creates are set in different places.

definition: The object a Deployment uses to keep an exact number of matching Pods running.
watch_for: Edit the Deployment, not its ReplicaSet; the Deployment will undo direct changes.

definition: A controller for Pods that need stable names and their own storage, such as databases.
watch_for: Stable names do not copy data between Pods or make a database highly available by themselves.

definition: A controller that runs one copy of a Pod on each suitable node, often for logging or networking agents.
watch_for: Nodes with taints the Pod does not tolerate are skipped.

definition: A controller that runs Pods until a task finishes successfully.
watch_for: Failed attempts are retried, so the task may run more than once; make it safe to repeat.

definition: A controller that creates Jobs on a schedule, like cron on Linux.
watch_for: A schedule does not guarantee the work happens exactly once per run.

definition: A named area inside a cluster for grouping objects and applying permissions and quotas.
watch_for: Namespaces do not block network traffic between Pods unless NetworkPolicies say so.

definition: A rule that picks objects by their labels, such as app=dispatch. Services and Deployments use them to find Pods.
watch_for: A selector can be perfectly valid and still match no Pods at all.

definition: A stable name and address in Kubernetes that forwards traffic to a changing set of matching Pods.
watch_for: Its name can resolve even when no ready Pods are behind it, so requests still fail.

definition: The list of Pod addresses a Service is currently sending traffic to, with whether each is ready.
watch_for: Check it when a Service exists but requests fail: an empty list means no Pods were selected or ready.

definition: A Service type that opens the same port on every node and forwards it to the Service’s Pods.
watch_for: The port is on the node machines, not automatically on your own computer.

definition: A set of HTTP routing rules, such as which hostname or path goes to which Service.
watch_for: It does nothing without an ingress controller running in the cluster to carry out the rules.

definition: A newer set of Kubernetes routing objects (GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute) that splits infrastructure from app routing.
watch_for: An accepted route still needs a real request to confirm it works.

definition: A Kubernetes object holding ordinary settings that Pods can read as files or environment variables.
watch_for: Environment variables are read only when a container starts; restart Pods after changing them.

definition: A Kubernetes object for sensitive values such as passwords, with separate access controls.
watch_for: Its values are base64 encoded, not encrypted; anyone allowed to read the Secret can decode them.

definition: An identity that a Pod uses when it talks to the Kubernetes API.
watch_for: Having an identity does not grant permissions; RBAC decides what it may do.

definition: Role-based access control: Roles list allowed actions, and RoleBindings give those roles to users or service accounts.
watch_for: A RoleBinding only grants access inside its own namespace; use a ClusterRoleBinding for the whole cluster.

definition: A Kubernetes rule that says which Pods may send traffic to which other Pods or addresses.
watch_for: It is only enforced if the cluster’s network plugin supports it; test allowed and blocked traffic.

definition: Pod or container settings that control its user, special permissions, and filesystem access.
watch_for: A read-only filesystem may still need a small writable folder, such as /tmp, for the app to work.

definition: A Linux feature that limits which low-level system operations a process may request.
watch_for: It narrows what a process can do but does not replace running as a non-root user.

definition: The amount of CPU and memory a container asks for; Kubernetes uses it to decide which node has room.
watch_for: A CPU request is not a cap; a container can use more CPU if it is free.

definition: The most CPU or memory a container is allowed to use.
watch_for: Going over a CPU limit slows the container down; going over a memory limit gets it killed.

definition: A check that decides whether a Pod should receive traffic right now.
watch_for: Failing it removes the Pod from the Service but does not restart it.

definition: A check that tells Kubernetes to restart a container if it keeps failing.
watch_for: If it depends on a database, a database outage restarts every Pod and makes things worse.

definition: A check that gives a slow-starting app time before liveness and readiness checks begin.
watch_for: Set its allowance to cover how long the app really takes to start.

definition: A PersistentVolumeClaim: a Pod’s request for storage of a certain size and type.
watch_for: A claim stuck in Pending may be waiting for a Pod to be scheduled, not missing storage.

definition: A PersistentVolume: a piece of storage in the cluster that can be bound to one claim.
watch_for: Its reclaim policy decides what happens to the data when the claim is deleted; Retain keeps it but is not a backup.

definition: A named kind of storage, with the settings used to create volumes for claims automatically.
watch_for: WaitForFirstConsumer waits to create storage until a Pod using it is scheduled, so it lands on the right node.

definition: The Container Storage Interface: the standard way storage plugins connect to Kubernetes.
watch_for: A manually created local volume does not exercise a storage plugin at all.

definition: The Container Network Interface: the standard way network plugins give Pods their network connections.
watch_for: A node showing Ready does not prove Pods on different nodes can reach each other or resolve names.

definition: The Container Runtime Interface: how the kubelet asks a runtime such as containerd to run containers.
watch_for: crictl talks to that interface directly; ctr is containerd’s own lower-level tool.

definition: The agent on each node that starts the Pods assigned to it and reports their status.
watch_for: Containers keep running if the kubelet stops, but nothing on that node is updated or reported.

definition: A tool that sets up a Kubernetes cluster’s control plane and joins nodes to it.
watch_for: It does not install a network plugin or a load balancer for you.

definition: A Pod the kubelet runs directly from a file on the node, used for control-plane parts such as the API server.
watch_for: Deleting it through kubectl does nothing lasting; change or remove the file on the node instead.

definition: The database where Kubernetes stores all of its objects.
watch_for: An etcd backup does not include the data inside your applications’ volumes.

definition: The majority of members a group needs to agree before it can make changes.
watch_for: Three etcd members can survive one failure; adding a fourth does not let it survive two.

definition: The file kubectl reads to know which clusters exist, how to log in, and which one to use.
watch_for: It can contain keys and tokens, so treat it like a password file.

definition: The encryption used by HTTPS, which also proves the server is who it claims to be using certificates.
watch_for: Turning off certificate checks hides the problem instead of fixing it.

definition: A small Kubernetes object that is renewed regularly, used for node heartbeats and choosing leaders.
watch_for: A recently renewed lease is better evidence a node is alive than an old Ready status.

definition: The HorizontalPodAutoscaler: it adds or removes Pods automatically based on measurements such as CPU use.
watch_for: It needs resource requests on the Pods and a working metrics server to measure against.

definition: A package manager for Kubernetes that turns templates, called charts, into objects and tracks installed releases.
watch_for: Check the rendered objects and the running Pods, not just that Helm reported success.

definition: A tool built into kubectl that builds Kubernetes files from a shared base plus small per-environment changes.
watch_for: A patch can apply cleanly and still change the wrong field; look at the output of kubectl kustomize.

definition: A controller that knows how to run a particular application, usually managed through its own custom object types.
watch_for: Adding a custom object type does nothing until a controller acts on it.

definition: A way of working where a controller keeps the cluster matching files stored in Git.
watch_for: A manual fix in the cluster gets undone unless you also change Git.

definition: A service level objective: a target for how reliable a service should be, such as 99% of requests succeeding over 30 days.
watch_for: It needs a clear definition of good requests, total requests, and the time window to be measurable.

definition: A software bill of materials: a list of the components inside an image.
watch_for: Knowing what is inside is not the same as knowing it is free of security problems.

definition: Replacing a password or key, updating everything that uses it, and making sure the old one no longer works.
watch_for: Changing a Secret does not mean running Pods are using the new value yet.

definition: Actually restoring a backup somewhere safe and checking the data and application work.
watch_for: A backup command finishing without errors does not prove the backup can be restored.

definition: A taint on a node keeps Pods away unless they carry a matching toleration, which permits, but does not require, scheduling there.
watch_for: A toleration only allows a Pod onto a tainted node; add a nodeSelector or affinity if the Pod must run there.

definition: Rules in a Pod spec that require or prefer nodes with particular labels, a more expressive form of nodeSelector.
watch_for: requiredDuringScheduling rules can leave a Pod Pending forever if no node matches; preferred rules never block scheduling.

definition: A cluster-wide object giving Pods a priority number; when nodes are full, higher-priority Pods are scheduled first and can preempt lower ones.
watch_for: Pods only use a class that names it in priorityClassName; for a Deployment, set it in the Pod template.

definition: A rule limiting how many matching Pods voluntary disruptions, such as a node drain, may evict at once.
watch_for: A budget that allows zero disruptions makes kubectl drain wait forever; it does nothing about crashes or node failures.

definition: A container that runs to completion before a Pod’s main containers start, used for setup such as writing configuration or waiting for a dependency.
watch_for: If an init container keeps failing, the Pod stays in Init status and the main containers never start.

definition: A helper container that runs alongside the main container in the same Pod, sharing its network and volumes, for jobs such as shipping logs.
watch_for: Containers in one Pod share localhost and any mounted volumes, but each has its own filesystem otherwise.

definition: The program in a terminal that reads each command you type, fills in variables, and starts the program the command names.
watch_for: The shell treats some characters specially, such as $, <, >, |, and spaces, so quote values that contain them.

definition: A file or folder’s location. A relative path starts from your working directory; an absolute path starts at the top folder, written /.
watch_for: The same relative path means different files from different folders; check where you are with pwd.

definition: A named value that a process receives when it starts, such as DOCKYARD_PORT in your lab terminal or DB_HOST inside a container.
watch_for: A running process keeps the values it started with; changing the variable later does not reach it until it restarts.

definition: The two channels a program prints to: one for normal output and one for error messages. Docker keeps both as a container’s logs.
watch_for: Redirecting with > captures only standard output; add 2>&1 to capture error messages too.

definition: The number a process leaves when it finishes: 0 for success and anything else for a reported problem. A stopped container shows it as Exited (N).
watch_for: Exit status 0 means the program reported success, not that it produced the result you wanted.

definition: A text format for structured settings, built from mappings of keys to values, lists, and single values, with indentation showing what belongs to what.
watch_for: Indentation changes meaning without any warning, and unquoted values such as 1.0 or yes may not stay as text.

definition: A file, usually YAML, that describes the objects you want, such as a Deployment and a Service, so a tool can create or update them to match.
watch_for: Applying a manifest records what you want; check the running objects to see whether it happened.

definition: The three-digit number at the start of an HTTP response: 2xx means success, 4xx a problem with the request, and 5xx a problem on the server.
watch_for: Any status, even 500, means the request arrived and the server answered; connection errors happen before there is a status.

definition: A number that picks one service on a machine. A server listens on a port, and a client connects to an address and a port together.
watch_for: A listening port shows that something accepts connections, not that the application behind it is ready.

definition: The name for 127.0.0.1, which always means the machine or container making the request.
watch_for: Inside a container, localhost is that container, not your computer or a neighbouring container.

definition: The Domain Name System, which turns a name such as dispatch into an address. In a cluster, CoreDNS answers names for Services.
watch_for: A name that resolves only proves the lookup worked; the connection and the application still need checking.

definition: The stable virtual address Kubernetes gives a normal Service. Traffic sent to it is forwarded to one of the Service’s ready Pods.
watch_for: A ClusterIP exists even when no Pod is ready, so connecting to it can still fail.

definition: A Service with clusterIP: None. Instead of one virtual address, DNS returns the Pods’ own addresses, giving each StatefulSet Pod its own name.
watch_for: A headless Service does no load balancing of its own; clients connect to Pod addresses directly.

definition: The node component that programs each node’s network rules so traffic to a Service’s ClusterIP reaches one of its Pods.
watch_for: Rules kube-proxy already wrote can keep working after it stops; test with a newly created Service.

definition: A kernel feature that gives a process its own view of something, such as the process list, the network, or the files. Containers are built from them.
watch_for: This is different from a Kubernetes namespace, which groups objects inside a cluster.

definition: A control group: a kernel feature that measures and limits the memory, CPU, and number of processes a group of processes may use.
watch_for: A container that reaches its memory limit is killed, while one that reaches its CPU limit is slowed down.

definition: The numeric user and group IDs Linux uses to decide what a process may do. UID 0 is root.
watch_for: Linux checks the numbers, not the names, so a container’s UID 10001 must match the owner of the files it writes.

definition: A file’s permissions: read, write, and execute, set separately for its owner, its group, and everyone else, such as -rw-r----- or 640.
watch_for: chmod 777 lets every user change the file; give the one user that needs access exactly what it needs.

definition: The Linux service manager that starts background services, restarts them if they fail, and collects their logs for journalctl.
watch_for: active (running) means the process is running, not that the service works or uses your latest settings.

definition: A short message the kernel delivers to a process. SIGTERM asks it to stop cleanly; SIGKILL ends it immediately and cannot be ignored.
watch_for: A process that ignores SIGTERM is killed when the grace period ends, without finishing its work.

definition: The background service that stores images and creates and runs containers. The docker command sends it requests.
watch_for: If the engine is not running, every docker command fails, even though the docker command itself is installed.

definition: The thin layer each container adds on top of its image’s read-only layers. Files a container creates or changes are stored there.
watch_for: Removing the container deletes its writable layer; keep data that must survive in a volume or bind mount.

definition: A text file of instructions, such as FROM, COPY, RUN, and CMD, that docker build follows to make an image.
watch_for: Editing a Dockerfile changes nothing until you rebuild the image and replace the running container.

definition: A readable name for an image version, such as dispatch:release, written after a colon in an image reference.
watch_for: A tag can be moved to a different image at any time; use a digest when you need exactly the same content.

definition: The operating system and processor type an image is built for, such as linux/arm64 or linux/amd64. One image name can cover several platforms.
watch_for: An image built only for another processor type may fail to start or run slowly under emulation.

definition: The background job application supplied with this course: an API that accepts jobs, a queue, workers that process them, and a database that stores them.
watch_for: Dispatch grows through the course; each lab says which parts exist at that stage.

definition: The front door of a Kubernetes cluster. kubectl, controllers, and kubelets all read and change cluster objects through it, and it stores them in etcd.
watch_for: The API server accepting a change means it was stored, not that Pods are already running.

definition: kubectl port-forward listens on a port on your computer and tunnels each connection through the API server to one Pod, chosen from a Service if you name one.
watch_for: It reaches a single Pod and stops when the command ends; it is for testing, not for real users.

definition: The Deployment strategy that replaces old Pods with new ones a few at a time, within limits set by maxSurge and maxUnavailable.
watch_for: A rollout stuck on a bad image can leave old Pods serving while the update never finishes; check rollout status.

definition: Running a small number of copies of a new release beside the stable one, so a share of real traffic tests it before everyone gets it.
watch_for: With Service-based splitting, the share follows the Pod count, not an exact percentage.

definition: Running the new release fully beside the old one, then switching all traffic at once, for example by changing a Service’s selector.
watch_for: It needs room for two full copies, and switching back is fast only while the old copy is still running.

definition: The quality of service class Kubernetes gives a Pod from its requests and limits: Guaranteed, Burstable, or BestEffort.
watch_for: When a node runs short of memory, BestEffort Pods are evicted first and Guaranteed Pods last.

definition: A scheduling rule that keeps copies of a workload spread across nodes or zones, within a maximum difference called maxSkew.
watch_for: Without one, the scheduler may place every copy on the same node, so one node failure stops them all.

definition: Cordoning marks a node so no new Pods are scheduled there; draining also evicts its Pods so they are replaced elsewhere before maintenance.
watch_for: A drain waits for PodDisruptionBudgets, and Pods with local data cannot simply move to another node.

definition: A short record of something Kubernetes noticed about an object, such as Scheduled, Pulled, or a failed probe, shown by kubectl describe.
watch_for: Events expire after a while, so look soon after a problem and keep other evidence for later.

definition: A number measured over time, such as requests served or memory used, collected by tools such as Prometheus.
watch_for: A metric shows how much or how often, not why; pair it with logs and events to explain a change.

definition: A metric that only goes up, such as the total number of requests, and resets to zero when its process restarts.
watch_for: Read a counter through rate() over a time window; its raw value says little on its own.

definition: A metric that counts observations, such as request durations, in cumulative buckets like at or under 0.1 seconds.
watch_for: Each bucket includes everything below it, so subtract buckets to count requests between two limits.

definition: A rule that watches a condition in metrics and notifies people when it stays true for long enough: pending first, then firing, then resolved.
watch_for: An alert that fires on every brief blip trains people to ignore it; set a sensible waiting period.

definition: The number of bad events an objective allows. An SLO of 95% good over 200 requests leaves a budget of 10 bad ones.
watch_for: Slow successful requests can count as bad if the objective includes speed.

definition: An automated series of stages, such as build, test, push, and record, that every change passes through on its way to running.
watch_for: A stage that is skipped or always passes gives false confidence; check that a failing test really stops the pipeline.

definition: A built-in check that accepts or rejects new Pods in a namespace against a standard such as restricted, when they are created.
watch_for: It checks only at creation; Pods that are already running are not changed or removed.

definition: A block of addresses written as a starting address and a size, such as 10.244.0.0/16. Clusters use separate ranges for nodes, Pods, and Services.
watch_for: If the Pod range overlaps the node network, traffic goes to the wrong place even though nodes show Ready.

definition: A repeatable way to find a fault: observe the symptom, guess one cause, test it, change one thing, and check whether the symptom changed.
watch_for: Changing several things at once hides which change mattered, and can add a new fault.

definition: A way for a Pod to pass facts about itself, such as its name, namespace, node, labels, and resource limits, into its own containers as environment variables or files.
watch_for: Environment variables are fixed when the container starts; only files from a downwardAPI volume follow changes such as new labels.

definition: When a higher-priority Pod cannot fit on any node, the scheduler removes enough lower-priority Pods from one node to make room for it.
watch_for: Preempted Pods are recreated by their controllers and wait as Pending; preemption decides which work waits, it does not scale anything down.

definition: A rule written as a CEL expression that the API server checks when objects are created or updated; a binding puts it into effect for chosen resources and namespaces.
watch_for: A policy without a binding refuses nothing, and a binding with Warn or Audit only reports; only Deny refuses the request.

definition: A temporary container added to a Pod that is already running, usually to bring debugging tools the application's image leaves out.
watch_for: It never restarts and cannot be removed; it disappears only when the Pod is replaced.
